message:
feat(live): shared-player hand-off for the classic Live browse fullscreen (no reload)

The classic 3-column Live browse screen used to RELEASE the preview player before
launching fullscreen and RECONNECT the stream from scratch — then reconnect AGAIN on
the way back. The EPG guide screen already had a proven zero-reconnect hand-off
(LiveSharedPlayer); this ports it to the classic screen.

- launchFullscreen: instead of previewPanel.releasePlayer(), capture the last preview
  frame + detachPlayer() + LiveSharedPlayer.offer(...) and launch with
  sharedLivePlayer=true. PlayerActivity ADOPTS that exact running player (same provider
  socket, no reconnect). max_connections=1 is never violated — there is never a moment
  with two open connections (the socket travels, it is not duplicated). Falls back to a
  cold start when there is no preview player to hand off.
- handleLivePlayerResult: adopt the player back into the preview (adoptPlayer) instead of
  play()-ing fresh, so the channel does not reload on return either. Falls back to a fresh
  preview if nothing was handed back.
- PreviewPlayerPanel.captureFrame(): snapshot the TextureView for the hand-off cover.
- LiveSharedPlayer.isParked(): a player is awaiting adoption.

RACE FIX: on the classic screen, LiveEpgPreviewController.maybeRestorePreviewFromState
(onResume) could occasionally reconnect a fresh preview from watch-history BEFORE the
result callback adopted the handed-back player — the "sometimes it reloads on return"
the owner reported. It now defers when LiveSharedPlayer.isParked() (the fullscreen exit
always pairs a parked player with RESULT_OK, so handleLivePlayerResult restores it
authoritatively).

Lightweight LIVE_HANDOFF diagnostics (Log.i, once per fullscreen transition) on this
incident-prone path.

Device-verified on .35 (owner QA): ~6 enter/exit cycles across channels — every return
logged "ADOPTED back (no reload)", ZERO "FRESH play (reload)", zero 403 / connection-limit
/ AudioTrack / ExoPlayer errors, no crash. Audio + favourites confirmed working. Any
residual occasional buffering is provider/network-side (the live stream itself), not a
client reconnect. Clean build + unit tests + detekt green.

Follow-up (not in this commit): the literal zoom grow/shrink transition (Part B).
